content: Enalapril Maleate Dosing Information 1. Treatment with Diuretics: Initial dosage: 2.5 mg for at least 4 hours. 2. Treatment without Diuretics: Initial dose for patients not receiving a diuretic: Usual dosage range: Enalapril 10–40 mg orally per day, divided into two doses. The maximum dose is 40 mg/day, adjusted based on response. 3. Important Considerations: If possible, discontinue diuretics for 2–3 days before starting therapy with Vasotec (Enalapril). In some patients treated once daily, the antihypertensive effect may diminish toward the end of the dosing interval. In such cases, consider increasing the dosage or administering the medication twice daily. Concomitant use of Vasotec with potassium supplements, potassium salt substitutes, or potassium-sparing diuretics may lead to increased serum potassium levels. Dosage Adjustment in Hypertensive Patients with Renal Impairment 1. For patients with creatinine clearance >30 mL/min (serum creatinine up to approximately 3 mg/dL): Follow standard dosing guidelines. 2. For patients with creatinine clearance ≤30 mL/min (serum creatinine ≥3 mg/dL): Initial dosage: 2.5 mg orally once daily. Maximum dosage: Asymptomatic Left Ventricular Dysfunction 1. Initial dosage: 2.5 mg orally twice daily. 2. Targeted daily dose: 20 mg/day in divided doses. 3. Monitoring: 4. Diuretic Adjustment: If possible, reduce the dose of any concomitant diuretic to minimize the likelihood of hypotension. 5. Hypotension Management: The occurrence of hypotension after the initial dose does not preclude subsequent careful dose titration following effective management of the hypotension. Dosage Adjustment in Patients with Heart Failure and Renal Impairment or Hyponatremia 1. For patients with heart failure and hyponatremia (serum sodium <130 mEq/L) or serum creatinine >1.6 mg/dL: Initial dosage: 2.5 mg/day under close medical supervision. Maximum dosage: 40 mg/day, with gradual dose increases. Pediatric Hypertensive Patients 1. Usual recommended starting dose: 0. Doses above 0.58 mg/kg (or exceeding 40 mg) have not been studied in pediatric patients. 2. Neonates and Pediatric Patients with Severe Renal Impairment: Vasotec is not recommended for neonates or pediatric patients with a glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73 m² due to a lack of data. Myocardial Infarction Developed by the American College of Cardiology Foundation (ACCF) and the American Heart Association (AHA). Class of Recommendation: Class IIa. Level of Evidence: Not applicable. Cardiomyopathy Dosage: 2.5 mg or 5 mg orally once or twice daily. Aortic Valve Regurgitation Dosage: 20 mg/day or 20 mg twice daily. Chyluria Dosage: 5 mg twice daily. Prophylaxis Treatment of Diabetes Mellitus Dosage: 5–20 mg/day. Diabetic Nephropathy Dosage: 5 mg/day, with potential increases to 10 mg/day as needed. Direct Current Cardioversion Dosage: 10 mg orally twice daily, up to 20 mg twice daily. Erythrocytosis Dosage: 15 mg three times daily or 5 mg once daily, with a maximum of 20 mg/day. Refractory to Diuretic Therapy Initial dose: Enalapril 0.1 mg/kg/day orally. Alport Syndrome Dosage: 40 mg/day. Prophylaxis Treatment of Migraine Dosage: 10–25 mg/day. Neurally-Mediated Syncope Dosage: 10 mg/day. Renovascular Hypertension Dosage: 5 mg/day. Patients with Hereditary or Idiopathic Angioedema Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, including Enalapril, may affect the metabolism of eicosanoids and polypeptides, such as endogenous bradykinin, potentially leading to adverse reactions, some of which may be serious. Head and Neck Angioedema Angioedema involving the face, extremities, lips, tongue, glottis, and/or larynx has been reported in patients treated with ACE inhibitors, including Enalapril. This may occur at any time during treatment. If angioedema occurs, discontinue Enalapril immediately and provide appropriate therapy and monitoring until complete resolution of symptoms. Intestinal Angioedema Intestinal angioedema has been reported in patients treated with ACE inhibitors. Symptoms include abdominal pain, with or without nausea or vomiting, and may occur without prior facial angioedema. Diagnosis is confirmed via imaging or surgery, and symptoms resolve upon discontinuation of the ACE inhibitor. Anaphylactoid Reactions During Desensitization Life-threatening anaphylactoid reactions have been reported in patients undergoing desensitization treatment with hymenoptera venom while receiving ACE inhibitors. These reactions were avoided when ACE inhibitors were temporarily withheld. Hypotension Excessive hypotension is rare in uncomplicated hypertensive patients treated with Enalapril alone. Therapy discontinuation is usually unnecessary if dosing instructions are followed. Neutropenia/Agranulocytosis Rare cases of neutropenia and agranulocytosis have been reported, particularly in patients with renal impairment or collagen vascular disease. Periodic monitoring of white blood cell counts is recommended in such patients. Hepatic Failure Rarely, ACE inhibitors have been associated with a syndrome beginning with cholestatic jaundice and progressing to fulminant hepatic necrosis, sometimes resulting in death. Discontinue ACE inhibitors if jaundice or significant elevations in hepatic enzymes occur. Fetal/Neonatal Morbidity and Mortality ACE inhibitors can cause fetal and neonatal harm when administered to pregnant women. Discontinue ACE inhibitors as soon as pregnancy is detected. Adverse Experiences Common adverse effects include hypotension, cough, hyperkalemia, and renal dysfunction. Serious adverse effects, such as angioedema and hepatic failure, are rare but require immediate medical attention.
